11604.short: Raiders coach Klink Kubiak said after Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos that he's optimistic Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) will be available to face the Browns on Nov. 29, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
11604.long: Bowers "was not ready to play" against Denver, per Kubiak, but the head coach believes Vegas' star tight end could be ready to return in Week 12 against the Browns on SNF. Bowers was held to 18 yards by the Seahawks during Fernando Mendoza's first regular-season start in Week 10 after mustering at least 70 receiving yards in each of his seven games with Kirk Cousins.

12689.short: Pegues is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Broncos due to a forearm injury.
12689.long: Pegues managed to log one tackle across 30 defensive snaps before exiting late in the fourth quarter. He's the third defensive lineman for the Raiders to be injured against Denver.

13558.short: Keenan (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against Denver.
13558.long: Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

4415.short: Butler (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
4415.long: Butler took a blow to the head late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end due to a concussion. With Tim Keenan (knee) also done for the night, JJ Pegues is the last man standing at defensive tackle for Las Vegas.

8527.short: Young (stinger) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against Denver.
8527.long: Young suffered a stinger late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now in question. In his absence, Cody White is a candidate to see a slight uptick in opportunities on offense with Las Vegas.

12541.short: Thornton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Denver.
12541.long: Thornton is dealing with a back injury, but he wasn't listed on Las Vegas' practice report during Week 11 prep. As such, it appears the second-year wideout is a healthy scratch Sunday. Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech, Dareke Young and Cody White will make up the Raiders' WR corps.

5090.short: Fatukasi (toe) is active against the Broncos on Sunday.
5090.long: Fatukasi was tagged as questionable due to a toe injury, although he ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, and he's now been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. The veteran defensive lineman has 16 tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games.

6083.short: Gay (hip) is active for Sunday's game at Denver.
6083.long: Gay sandwiched two limited practices this week around Thursday's DNP due to a right hip injury and entered the weekend listed as questionable for Sunday. Because the Raiders didn't elevate Kansei Matsuzawa from the practice squad Saturday, it was an indication that Gay was good to go for Week 11, which now has been confirmed. In 10 games this season, Gay has connected on 21 of 23 field-goal attempts and all 22 point-after tries.

13122.short: The Raiders elevated Runyon from the practice squad Saturday.
13122.long: Las Vegas is bringing up Runyon due to Brock Bowers (ankle) being listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Runyon appeared in 13 games with the Raiders last season but logged just 45 offensive snaps and caught only one pass for three yards. He's depth behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas.

8380.short: Booker (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
8380.long: An ankle injury has sidelined Booker for each of the Raiders' last two games. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that he's recovered from his injury and on track to play in Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Broncos. Booker has accumulated 13 tackles (nine solo) across seven regular-season games.

7633.short: Paye (neck) was not listed on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
7633.long: Paye made an early exit in the second half of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks with a neck injury. The linebacker did not return to the contest, but the issue does not seem to have been serious. Paye is healthy and appears ready to log consistent full practices throughout Week 11 prep.

9754.short: Johnston caught one of two targets for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets. He added one yard on one rushing attempt.
9754.long: Johnston was targeted on just 9.5 percent of Justin Herbert's 21 pass attempts against New York. The wideout has now caught exactly one pass in three straight games and five of his last six contests. Johnston is nothing more than a lightly-targeted deep threat who will continue to see fewer looks if Ladd McConkey is able to maintain his health for an extended period.

11647.short: Vidal carried the ball seven times for 36 yards and caught both his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
11647.long: After handling just four touches last week against the Ravens, Vidal saw his usage increase again as he recorded his most scrimmage yards since Week 5. This time, however, his additional volume came at the expense of Keaton Mitchell (knee), who left the game early. Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the Chargers' clear No. 1 RB over the last few contests, but if Mitchell's injury proves to be serious, Vidal could have some deeper-league appeal with the No. 2 role all to himself. He'll look to take advantage of whatever opportunities he gets in Week 12 against the Patriots.

12509.short: Harris caught both his targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
12509.long: With Ladd McConkey back in the lineup, Harris' role in the passing attack shrank after he'd turned 12 targets over the prior two games into an 8-92-0 line. Harris' fantasy appeal would collapse even further if Justin Herbert (concussion) ends up missing any time. The second-year wideout will at least get a promising matchup in Week 12 against a vulnerable Patriots' secondary.

11635.short: McConkey caught five of eight targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
11635.long: His longest gain went for just 11 yards, but McConkey was deadly in the red zone, connecting with Justin Herbert on scores of 11 and six yards in the fourth quarter as the Chargers tried to mount a late comeback. Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol after the game after taking six sacks, and if he end up missing any time, it would put a big damper on McConkey's fantasy outlook with undrafted rookie DJ Uiagalelei being the Bolts' backup, unless Trey Lance (groin) is able to return from IR. McConkey has had plenty of trouble staying on the field himself this year, of course, and he'll take a 22-323-3 line on 32 targets through seven contests into a Week 12 clash with the Patriots.

12507.short: Hampton carried the ball 14 times for 89 yards and caught his only target for four yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
12507.long: While he's still not seeing a consistent bell-cow workload, Hampton has turned his season around over the last three games, racking up 254 rushing yards and a TD while averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell left Sunday's game early with a knee injury, but his absence appeared to provide a bigger boost to Kimani Vidal, who wound up getting nine touches and 54 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against the Patriots.

6797.short: Herbert entered the concussion protocol after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
6797.long: Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in Week 11, but he also endured six sacks, fumbled once and added 32 yards and one TD on his eight carries. It's unclear exactly when he picked up the head injury, but he'll be subject to the concussion protocol ahead of further game action. The Chargers take the field next Sunday against the Patriots.

13341.short: Mesidor (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
13341.long: Mesidor suffered an ankle injury during the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In the rookie's absence, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree are both candidates to see an increase in opportunities at outside linebacker behind starters Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack.

9511.short: Mitchell (back) has re-entered Sunday's game against the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
9511.long: Mitchell temporarily exited the contest in the first half due to a back issue. However, he's since returned to the game as part of the kickoff-return unit. Mitchell is thus set to resume his usual role as both a backup RB and special-teams ace.

4033.short: Njoku (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
4033.long: Njoku briefly exited in the first quarter after hurting his shoulder on a 13-yard catch. He was initially deemed questionable to return but has since re-entered the contest. The veteran tight end is playing just his second game after returning from a stint on IR due to a fibula injury.

13131.short: Waxter (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
13131.long: Waxter was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. His availability gives the Chargers another contributor on special teams and depth in the secondary.

11779.short: Still is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets due to an ankle injury.
11779.long: Still wasn't on the Chargers' practice report until Friday, when he was a limited participant due to an ankle injury. Though he was initially deemed questionable, the third-year cornerback isn't going to be able to suit up against New York. Still's next chance to play will be in Week 12 against New England on Sunday, Nov. 29.

13380.short: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
13380.long: Thompson's inactive status doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he entered the weekend as doubtful due to a hamstring injury. He hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders, and his next chance to see the field is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

12670.short: Lambert-Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
12670.long: With Ladd McConkey (back) active, Lambert-Smith will be a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Lambert-Smith's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29, although his path to playing time is limited unless there is an injury in front of him on the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart.

8127.short: Kolar (concussion) is active for Sunday's game versus the Jets.
8127.long: Kolar showed up on the Chargers' first Week 11 injury report Wednesday as a non-participant due to a concussion, and thereafter he managed just one limited session Friday before the team tagged him as questionable for Sunday. Despite his inability to practice fully this week and the prospect of gaining clearance from an independent neurologist shaped up as a difficult combination to overcome, he's available to the offense. Kolar will join Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku as L.A.'s active tight ends this weekend.

13633.short: The Chargers placed Shelley (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
13633.long: Shelley was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets due to an ankle injury. His placement on IR means he must miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the 49ers on Thursday, Dec. 17. Shelley has contributed both on defense and special teams and has eight solo tackles and a pass defense across six regular-season games.

2327.short: Dupree requested his release from the Chargers earlier this week, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
2327.long: Dupree also asked for a trade earlier in the season, but the Chargers have so far not granted his request. The veteran edge rusher has been limited to special teams over the Chargers' last two games and has yet to record a sack. If he's let go by the Chargers, then Dupree could garner interest from teams looking for a boost in the pass rush.

11743.short: Eboigbe (ankle) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
11743.long: Eboigbe was unable to play against the Ravens this past Monday due to an ankle injury. He ended Week 11 prep with a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. His return means there will be less rotational snaps at defensive end for rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett.

4092.short: Tomlinson recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
4092.long: In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

6348.short: Phillips recorded nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
6348.long: Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

8259.short: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
8259.long: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

7136.short: Curl (toe) did not practice Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
7136.long: Curl played through the issue last week against the Cardinals and should be fine for Wednesday's game against the Packers assuming he didn't suffer any setbacks versus Arizona. Curl has started all 10 games this season, recording 48 tackles (28 solo) and three pass breakups.

3973.short: Garrett (knee) was limited in practice Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
3973.long: With the Rams playing the Packers on Wednesday, the team was required to release an injury report Sunday. Garrett is in no danger of missing Week 12. He has 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble across three games this season.

8150.short: Williams (toe) was a limited practice participant Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
8150.long: Head coach Sean McVay relayed to Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Saturday that Williams is dealing with a sore toe, so his practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep aren't a surprise. Williams will have two more chances to put himself in a position to avoid a designation for Wednesday's game against the Packers.

2133.short: Adams (hamstring) has an "outside chance" to return from injured reserve for the Rams' Week 13 matchup with the Chiefs but is more likely to be activated around mid-December, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
2133.long: The Rams have seemingly discounted the possibility of Adams coming off IR for a Wednesday matchup with the Packers in Week 12, while a Week 13 return is more plausible but still sounds like a "long shot," according to Rapoport. Instead, the Rams' Week 14 game against the 49ers on Dec. 13 would appear to be the most realistic target for Adams' return, especially since Los Angeles will effectively have a "mini-bye" ahead of that contest following its Thursday night matchup with Kansas City on Dec. 3. Whenever he's reinstated from IR, Adams should be in store for heavy target shares in the Rams' remaining games after star wideout Puka Nacua (knee) underwent season-ending MCL surgery earlier this week.

9493.short: Nacua (knee/toe) is expected to be sidelined 4-to-5 months after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his right MCL, which means he won't be on track to return at any point during the playoffs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
9493.long: Nacua is also dealing with a PCL sprain and turf toe, but the only procedure he required was for his MCL. With a firmer 4-to-5-month timeline now in place for the star wideout, he'll be done for the season while the Rams look to others to help fill the massive void in their receiver corps. Davante Adams (hamstring) should eventually take on a heavy target share, but he's also on injured reserve and isn't expected to return until at least Week 13. That leaves Konata Mumpfield, CJ Daniels, Tutu Atwell and Xavier Smith as the current healthy wideouts on the team's 53-man roster ahead of next Wednesday's tilt versus the Packers. Nacua, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is slated to become a free agent in March.

10916.short: The Rams designated Turner (groin) to return from injured reserve Saturday.
10916.long: Turner has missed the Rams' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. His practice participation over the coming days will ultimately determine whether he'll be activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

12718.short: The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Atkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report.
12718.long: Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angeles' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

12487.short: Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) isn't ready to return to game action, but the Rams still plan to activate him from injured reserve before Week 12 and keep him on the active roster, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
12487.long: Even if Ferguson is moved back to the active roster, coach Sean McVay's comments indicate the tight end still won't be ready to play coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. His activation at least would keep him off season-ending IR, but his near-term availability remains uncertain until the Rams signal he's ready for game action. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) likely done for the remainder of the regular season following MCL surgery, Ferguson and Davante Adams (hamstring) are needed badly in this offense.

8330.short: Lake posted two tackles (one solo) during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
8330.long: Lake recorded at least six tackles in each of the first nine games of the regular season, but he had only two stops in Week 10 despite playing every defensive snap. The fifth-year defensive back is up to 65 tackles (38 solo), 11 pass defenses (including three interceptions) and two forced fumbles through 10 regular-season games heading into the Week 11 bye.

13278.short: Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
13278.long: Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

13270.short: Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
13270.long: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

7562.short: Atwell caught one of two targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
7562.long: Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

8195.short: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
8195.long: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

10214.short: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
10214.long: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

1433.short: McManus made both of his field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
1433.long: McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

3271.short: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
3271.long: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

6865.short: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
6865.long: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

11610.short: Washington caught three of six targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills. He rushed two times for 11 yards.
11610.long: Washington's six targets were third on the team, trailing Caleb Douglas (10) and Greg Dulcich (seven) on a day Kyle McCord attempted 33 passes. Washington has just one touchdown this season and has yet to reach 70 receiving yards in any game in 2026. There's not much to like about the wideout's fantasy prospects moving forward this season.

8172.short: Dulcich caught two of seven targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
8172.long: Dulcich finished second on the team in targets behind wide receiver Caleb Douglas (10), but he failed to exceed 20 receiving yards for the third straight week. The tight end hasn't scored a touchdown this season, and his next chance will come in Week 12 against the Jets.

13296.short: Douglas caught two of 10 targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
13296.long: Douglas paced the team in targets and receiving yards, but he struggled to get on the same page as QB Kyle McCord, who completed just 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards. The rookie WR didn't help his cause with a red-zone drop in the third quarter. In Week 12, Douglas will face a Jets secondary against which he scored twice in their Week 7 matchup. Those are the only two touchdowns of his seven-game regular-season career.

12494.short: McCord completed 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills. He also rushed twice for nine yards.
12494.long: McCord has thrown for just 311 yards without a touchdown pass in his first two NFL starts. The 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles is poised to make at least two more starts while Malik Willis (abdomen) is on IR. Miami's lone win of the season came against the Jets, whom the Dolphins will host in Week 12.

12495.short: Gordon rushed 11 times for 69 yards while catching two of three targets for minus-2 yards in Sunday's 26-9 loss to the Bills.
12495.long: After a quiet first half, Gordon got free for a 24-yard run on the first possession of the second half to set up Miami's third and final field goal of the afternoon. Gordon was Miami's most effective offensive player as usual, as Kyle McCord threw for just 102 yards in the latter's second NFL start. This was Gordon's seventh consecutive game with at least 64 scrimmage yards, but he'll take a four-game touchdown drought into a Week 12 home game against the Jets.

10906.short: Brents (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's tilt against Buffalo.
10906.long: Brents was hurt in the fourth quarter and is uncertain to re-enter the contest. Darrell Baker has taken over for Brents at outside cornerback.

13311.short: Bell (chest) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
13311.long: Bell suffered a chest injury late in the first half and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. However, the rookie wideout got back into the game shortly after halftime. Bell will look to be more productive after finishing the first half without a reception.

11775.short: Simpson (knee) is listed as inactive for Sunday's matchup against the Bills.
11775.long: Simpson was previously doubtful for Sunday's game after not practicing Wednesday or Thursday and ending the week with limited participation. The 26-year-old plays the majority of snaps on special teams, so his absence shouldn't greatly impact the defense.

8666.short: Baker (knee) is active for Sunday's battle against the Bills.
8666.long: Baker had been on the reserve/PUP list all season before being activated Saturday. He logged a week of full practices, which led to the veteran cornerback being active for what will be his Dolphins debut Sunday. Baker may initially work in a rotational role behind starters JuJu Brents and Jason Marshall.

12673.short: Trader (shoulder/groin) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Buffalo.
12673.long: Trader's inactive status is not surprising given that he didn't practice all week and entered the weekend tagged as doubtful to suit up. Sunday will mark the second-year pro's first career absence. Kyle Louis and/or Zayne Anderson could get a big bump in work at safety in Trader's stead.

5095.short: The Dolphins elevated Carlson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
5095.long: Carlson signed with the Dolphins' practice squad Tuesday, two weeks after being released by the Saints. Following the Dolphins' release of Zane Gonzalez, Carlson will operate as Miami's kicker for Sunday's game against Buffalo. In seven appearances with the Saints this season, Carlson went 8-for-12 on field-goal attempts (including 3-for-7 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 16-for-18 on extra-point tries.

12679.short: Phillips underwent surgery on his injured bicep Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
12679.long: Phillips was recently placed on injured reserve with a season-ending biceps injury sustained in Week 10 versus the Colts. The 22-year-old ends his season with 28 tackles (11 solo) through nine games. Kenneth Grant and Keith Cooper are top candidates to see more reps at defensive tackle as the season continues.

6949.short: Brooks produced nine total tackles (six solo), a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
6949.long: Brooks was able to register at least nine takedowns for the fourth straight game and seventh time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to strip Colts running back Jonathan Taylor in the first quarter, but offensive lineman Dalton Tucker was able to jump on the loose ball. Brooks is now up to 84 total tackles (38 solo) while also adding two passes defensed and a forced fumble over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

13453.short: Rodriguez recorded one solo tackle during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
13453.long: Rodriguez finished with fewer than eight takedowns for just the third time this season, and his one tackle was a season low for the rookie. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (36 solo), including a 1.0 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over nine contests so far during his rookie campaign.

13517.short: Taaffe recorded six total tackles (four solo) and an interception during Sunday's 24-22 loss to the Colts.
13517.long: Taaffe was able to register at least six stops for the third straight game and sixth time overall this season. The safety's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter, when he jumped in front of a short pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, securing his third interception of the year. On the year, Taaffe has compiled 53 total tackles (27 solo), three interceptions and a forced fumble over nine contests so far.

12496.short: Felton caught six of 12 targets for 42 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
12496.long: Felton was set to operate in an expanded role with Jordan Addison (thumb) on injured reserve, and he garnered a game-high 12 targets. The wide receiver finished tied for second on the team in catches with tight end T.J. Hockenson while fellow wideout Justin Jefferson (seven) led the way. Felton has caught nine of 17 targets for 75 yards over the last two weeks, and his next chance to build off of his recent momentum will come in Week 12 against the Falcons.

8408.short: Mason rushed 11 times for 38 yards while catching his lone target for minus-1 yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
8408.long: Mason had one more carry and eight more rushing yards than Aaron Jones, but Jones' totals included an 11-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. They have worked in a near-even split when both veteran RBs have been healthy, but Mason hasn't scored since Week 1. Between his lack of TDs and minimal involvement as a pass catcher (three receptions for six yards in six games), Mason hasn't provided much fantasy value ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

4199.short: Jones rushed eight times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his lone target for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
4199.long: Jones tied the game with an 11-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, but the 49ers outscored the Vikings 21-3 in the second quarter, forcing Minnesota into a more pass-heavy approach. Jordan Mason led the team with 38 rushing yards on 11 carries. Jones and Mason should continue to split carries in Week 12 against the Falcons, with Jones offering greater upside as a pass catcher.

5844.short: Hockenson (wrist) caught six of seven targets for 55 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
5844.long: In his return from a one-game absence, Hockenson finished second on the team in receiving yards behind Justin Jefferson's 86. Hockenson showed promising chemistry with Kirk Cousins after the veteran TE sat out Cousins' return to Minnesota during the Week 10 win over Green Bay. Cousins was under center for the Vikings in the 2023 regular season, when Hockenson set career highs with 95 catches for 960 yards. Hockenson hasn't surpassed 455 yards in a regular season since, though he's on pace to do so this year, with 41 catches for 383 yards and three touchdowns through nine appearances heading into a Week 12 home game against the Falcons.

7049.short: Jennings caught three of six targets for 20 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
7049.long: Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.

1166.short: Cousins completed 26 of 38 passes for 235 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for no gain.
1166.long: After throwing a pick-six among his three interceptions when he faced San Francisco's defense in his final game with the Raiders in Week 9, Cousins had another interception returned for a touchdown by the 49ers in the second quarter of Sunday's loss. The Vikings took a 28-10 deficit into the halftime locker room, and Cousins was unable to orchestrate a comeback before Minnesota waved the white flag and inserted Carson Wentz for its final drive. Cousins is still strengthening his grasp on the offense two games into his reunion with the Vikings ahead of a Week 12 visit from the Falcons, with whom Cousins spent the previous two seasons.

6794.short: Jefferson caught seven of nine targets for 86 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
6794.long: Jefferson has experienced an uptick in usage since the Vikings reacquired Kirk Cousins. The star WR has 16 catches for 160 yards on 22 targets in two games with Cousins, though Jefferson hasn't scored since Week 8. Jefferson fumbled at the end of a 25-yard catch in the third quarter, turning what would have been one of his best plays of the night into a lowlight. Another heavy dose of targets from Cousins likely awaits Jefferson in Week 12 against the Falcons.

10939.short: Ward (knee) is inactive for Sunday night's game against the 49ers.
10939.long: The fourth-year safety has appeared in nine games this season but has logged just 17 snaps on defense while playing 162 on special teams.

7133.short: Rodgers (quadriceps) is inactive for Sunday night's matchup against the 49ers.
7133.long: Rodgers will be forced to miss Week 11 while nursing a quadriceps injury that forced him to log back-to-back limited practices to end the week. In his absence, Charles Demmings and Zemaiah Vaughn will both be in line to see increased opportunities in the secondary versus San Francisco.

12775.short: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but operating as the Vikings' emergency third QB on Sunday night versus the 49ers.
12775.long: Brosmer will operate as the team's No. 3 option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Kirk Cousins and primary backup Carson Wentz are forced out of the contest.

12700.short: Bartholomew should revert to a backup role with T.J. Hockenson returning from a wrist injury for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
12700.long: Bartholomew was targeted four times in Week 10 for three catches, 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers. The tight end received more than one target in only one other game this season, Week 5, when Hockenson went down after two offensive snaps. While Bartholomew has proven himself a red-zone threat, Hockenson should return to seeing most of the tight end volume in Sunday's contest.

11911.short: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
11911.long: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

6183.short: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
6183.long: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

6217.short: Cashman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
6217.long: Cashman will end up missing one game (Week 10 against the Packers) while in the league's concussion protocol, and his return means Ivan Pace will revert to a rotational role at inside linebacker for Sunday's contest. Cashman has accumulated 76 tackles (41 solo), including a career-high-tying 4.5 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery across eight regular-season games.

4413.short: Wilson recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10.
4413.long: The Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, with Wilson taking down the Packers quarterback for a six-yard loss early in the second quarter. Wilson has logged at least 0.5 sacks in three of his last four outings, and the veteran linebacker is up to 57 tackles (30 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense through nine regular-season games.

11929.short: The Vikings placed Richter (foot) on injured reserve Wednesday.
11929.long: Richter will now be forced to miss at least four games after suffering a foot injury during the Week 10 win over the Packers. The 26-year-old has compiled six tackles (three solo) across nine appearances this season while playing almost exclusively on special teams.

11792.short: Reichard made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers on Sunday.
11792.long: All three of Reichard's field goals came from fewer than 40 yards out in the contest. The return of Kirk Cousins allowed Minnesota's offense to surge to its highest touchdown total since Week 1, the team's first bout against the Packers. Reichard is now 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and remains perfect at 13-for-13 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

13075.short: Price is set for an increase in offensive workload with Jordan Addison (thumb) sidelined, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
13075.long: Price reeled in a season-high four passes for 49 yards and a score during Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. The wideout was operating in a more prominent offensive role for the second week in a row with Jauan Jennings (calf) sidelined, and fellow wide receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) was unable to play as well. Addison now is expected to undergo thumb surgery, opening the door for Price to operate in an elevated position in Minnesota's offense for the time being.

6901.short: Metellus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
6901.long: Metellus was added to the Vikings' practice report Friday due to a shoulder issue, but the injury won't prevent the seventh-year pro from suiting up for Sunday's NFC North showdown. He has 58 tackles (29 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and four pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

3161.short: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
3161.long: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

11564.short: Maye, who sustained a fractured right fibula in last Sunday's loss to the Lions, is on track to miss at least six weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
11564.long: The timetable put forth by Rapoport suggests that Maye could make a run at a late-season return, or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Given that the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve, Maye isn't a lock to land on IR, but he's nonetheless facing an absence longer than the required four games that a placement on IR would mandate. For now, Tommy DeVito has been installed as the team's starter ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup.

11292.short: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that DeVito will start in Week 12 against the Chargers on Nov. 29, Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN.com report.
11292.long: Drake Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, which he sustained in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich. DeVito filled in for the rest of that contest and completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning four carries into 19 yards. DeVito looks like he'll be New England's starter coming out of the bye, with rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton operating as the backup.

5859.short: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
5859.long: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

7921.short: Elliss logged 10 tackles (three solo) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
7921.long: Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

3233.short: Byard registered 10 tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
3233.long: Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

12547.short: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
12547.long: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

12969.short: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
12969.long: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

12542.short: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
12542.long: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

13421.short: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.
13421.long: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

12713.short: Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.
12713.long: Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.

9501.short: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
9501.long: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

3214.short: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
3214.long: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

4177.short: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
4177.long: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

12491.short: Kiner carried the ball 10 times for 25 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to Detroit.
12491.long: Rhamondre Stevenson was active despite dealing with a knee issue during the practice week, but the veteran back gained just four yards on six carries, and Kiner wound up leading the Patriots' backfield in both volume and yardage. The entire offense struggles after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, however. New England gets a Week 11 bye, so Kiner's role and usage for a Week 12 clash with the Chargers likely won't become clear until the health of Stevenson and Maye come into focus after the break.

7611.short: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
7611.long: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

5865.short: Jones (cramps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
5865.long: Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

5726.short: Spillane (illness) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
5726.long: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

4035.short: Kamara rushed one time for one yard and caught a one-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
4035.long: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. This three-man backfield continues to be one to try and avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

11834.short: Vele caught seven passes for 76 yards on seven targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
11834.long: Vele continues to run virtually every route for New Orleans, and the seven grabs matched his season high from Week 1 against the Lions, while Vele's 76 yards are a new high-water mark for the receiver. It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. This offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. Vele is more of a low-ceiling fantasy WR4/5 most weeks.

13281.short: Tyson caught one of two targets for six yards and added four rushing yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
13281.long: One week after logging 13 targets as Tyler Shough's top downfield option, Tyson all but disappeared as Chris Olave instead saw WR1-worthy volume. The Saints' aerial attack simply may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game, which would mark Tyson as a volatile, but high-ceiling, fantasy asset for the rest of the season. The rookie will try to bounce back in Week 12 against the Bengals.

7543.short: Etienne carried the ball 14 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 loss to Chicago.
7543.long: The former Jaguar was the clear No. 1 option in the backfield for the Saints. Alvin Kamara saw just two touches and CJ Donaldson handled five, although Kamara did vulture another red-zone TD on a one-yard reception in the second quarter, Most of Etienne's production came on a 46-yard scamper that saw him tackled just short of the goal line, setting up Kamara's score, but the fact that he was able to produce his first big play as a Saint was still encouraging. Etienne will attempt to build on this performance in Week 12 against the Bengals.

12545.short: Shough completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. He added 34 rushing yards on three carries.
12545.long: Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat. Shough has gone four straight games without producing multiple TDs, posting a 4:3 TD:INT over that stretch while completing 67.3 percent of his passes with a weak 6.3 YPA. The second-year QB will likely need to be a lot more productive in Week 12 if the Saints are going to keep up with Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

8144.short: Olave caught nine of 15 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
8144.long: One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.

7002.short: Johnson injured his hamstring during Sunday's game in Chicago, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
7002.long: Johnson visited the sideline tent in the third quarter before the Saints deemed him questionable to return. He didn't catch his only target before his departure.

7538.short: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday.
7538.long: As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.

7647.short: Werner (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against Chicago.
7647.long: Werner injured his hamstring against the Panthers in Week 10, and the injury prevented the sixth-year linebacker from practicing in any capacity during Week 11 prep. He was initially tagged as questionable, but he will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29. Danny Stutsman figures to start alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker in Werner's absence.

11579.short: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.
11579.long: Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

11653.short: The Saints signed Smyth to a two-year contract Saturday, Michael McQuaid of NFL Ireland reports.
11653.long: Smyth has been elevated from the Saints' practice squad for each of the team's last two games following the release of Daniel Carlson on Nov. 3. Smyth has gone 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 4-for-4 on extra-point tries in his two appearances, and his new deal means he'll be the Saints' kicker through the 2027 season.

13277.short: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
13277.long: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

6302.short: Elliss recorded 15 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
6302.long: Elliss was all over the field Sunday with a career-high 15 tackles (11 in the first half), which included an eight-yard sack on Bryce Young on the final play of the third quarter. Elliss has logged 10-plus tackles and a sack in back-to-back games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 56 stops (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across six regular-season games.

13420.short: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
13420.long: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

5857.short: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
5857.long: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

13387.short: The Saints placed Miller (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.
13387.long: Miller is dealing with a knee injury and is now required to miss at least four games. The rookie nose tackle has played in four games this season, logging five tackles (two solo) over 93 snaps on defense and four snaps on special teams. Nathan Shepherd and Khristian Boyd could both get more defensive snaps during Miller's absence.

11565.short: McCarthy completed 18 of 38 passes for 173 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions and rushed seven times for 33 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
11565.long: McCarthy had his share of trouble against an aggressive Jaguars defense, leading to a season-worst 47.4 percent completion rate. However, the emerging signal-caller avoided turnovers and connected with Malik Nabers for an eight-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter. McCarthy also provided some timely contributions with his legs, and he's averaging 5.4 yards on his 22 rush attempts to date. McCarthy connected with nine different targets overall as he continues to show good command of the offense, and he'll look to bounce back efficiency-wise in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

8131.short: Likely brought in one of three targets for 35 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
8131.long: Likely finished with season lows in reception and targets, although he did provide an impressive gain on his one catch. The breakout tight end was coming off a season-best 127-yard tally against the Commanders in Week 10, so Sunday's scant involvement can be described as an outlier. Despite the unremarkable performance, Likely still boasts a career-best 56-610-7 line across 10 games heading into a Week 12 road clash against the Colts next Sunday.

12481.short: Skattebo rushed 14 times for 34 yards and brought in three of seven targets for 14 yards in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
12481.long: Skattebo was unsurprisingly stymied on the ground by the Jaguars' elite run defense, and he couldn't really make up for it with his work through the air. Skattebo also committed another untimely turnover, fumbling at Jacksonville's 31-yard line with just over four minutes remaining in the third quarter and New York trying to add to a 20-6 lead. The change of possession ultimately didn't lead to any Jaguars points, however, and head coach John Harbaugh showed some faith in the second-year back by affording him the opportunity to ice the upset win with three carries on the final drive. Skattebo proved up to the task by netting 13 yards on those touches to force the Jags to exhaust their timeouts, and he should continue helming the backfield in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

11632.short: Nabers brought in seven of 12 targets for 55 yards and a touchdown in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday.
11632.long: Nabers was in the familiar position of leading the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and the third-year star also snapped a four-game touchdown drought with an eight-yard grab in the second quarter. Nabers has at least five catches in eight straight contests and three double-digit target tallies within that span, and the 2024 first-round pick should continue to be the subject of plenty of J.J. McCarthy's attention in a Week 12 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

7630.short: Newsome (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday evening's matchup with the Jaguars, Patricia Traina of SI.com reports.
7630.long: Newsome suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, and he will now officially remain sidelined for the rest of Week 11. In his absence, Paulson Adebo will continue to operate in an elevated role in New York's secondary.

12738.short: The Giants elevated Mafah from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
12738.long: It's the second time this season that Mafah has been promoted to the 53-man roster, with the first instance being Week 10 against the Eagles. His elevation gives the Giants another contributor on special teams and extra depth in the backfield behind Cam Skattebo, Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers.

6867.short: Harrison (groin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
6867.long: Harrison missed the Giants' contest versus the Commanders in Week 10 because of a groin injury, but it appears he'll be able to return to game action in Week 11. Of his 141 total snaps so far in 2026, 136 have come on special teams.

11655.short: Tracy (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve when first eligible ahead of the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
11655.long: The Giants haven't provided any updates on Tracy since he landed on IR on Oct. 27 after sustaining a hamstring strain in a Week 7 win over the Texans, but the running back is seemingly progressing well and could be ready to play once he sits out the required four games. Once he's reinstated, Tracy could operate as a change-of-pace option behind Cam Skattebo, who appears to have reclaimed the lead role out of the New York backfield after a one-game benching in Week 6.

2306.short: Winston carried twice for one yard in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
2306.long: J.J. McCarthy made his third consecutive start for the Giants, but Winston continued to get sprinkled into the game plan during short-yardage situations. He extended a second-quarter drive that culminated in a Cam Skattebo touchdown by gaining a yard on a fourth-and-one play, but Winston was dropped for no gain on a third-and-one run in the fourth quarter that resulted in a Giants punt. The Giants may continue to turn to Winston for quarterback sneaks in future weeks in an effort to limit the wear and tear on McCarthy.

11306.short: Gipson was signed by the Giants off of Philadelphia's practice squad Monday, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
11306.long: Gipson will head to New York after spending the entirety of the 2026 campaign to this point on the Eagles' practice squad. The Giants waived primary kick and punt returner Charlie Jones on Monday, and Gipson will likely take over that role beginning in Week 11 against the Jaguars.

8396.short: McFadden made 10 tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
8396.long: McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.

7666.short: Holland logged three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
7666.long: Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.

7970.short: Washington accumulated seven tackles (five solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
7970.long: Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.

13377.short: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
13377.long: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

13833.short: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.
13833.long: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

12498.short: Taylor caught two passes for 25 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
12498.long: The Jets controlled this game from start to finish and never trailed, so Geno Smith attempted just 21 passes to 37 run plays for New York. Taylor's 25 yards were his most in a game since Week 7, and he's totaled just 10 catches for 75 yards and no touchdowns over his last four contests. He's not a viable fantasy tight end.

11571.short: Davis didn't play an offensive snap in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
11571.long: As has been the case for three straight weeks. With Breece Hall back healthy, Davis has been glued to special teams for the Jets. He has no fantasy appeal.

13330.short: Sadiq caught all three of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
13330.long: Sadiq finished tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Adonai Mitchell and running back Breece Hall behind wideout Garrett Wilson (five). The tight end was able to reel in multiple passes for just the second time since catching seven of eight targets for 105 yards and a score in Week 3 against the Lions. Sadiq has now caught 25 of 36 targets for 268 yards and a score while also adding a three-yard rushing touchdown over the first 11 regular-season contests of his career.

11625.short: Mitchell caught two passes for 30 yards on three targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
11625.long: Even with Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Mitchell's role didn't change, as his three targets tied with two other teammates for second on the team behind Garrett Wilson's five on a day the Jets called 37 run plays to just 22 passes. Mitchell has just one touchdown this season and has only 14 catches for 212 yards and no touchdowns in six games surrounding his 7-142-1 receiving performance from Week 8 against the Raiders. He's a big-play specialist in an offense that prefers to feed Wilson and its running backs.

3200.short: Shepard caught two passes for 24 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
3200.long: With Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Shepard was elevated from the practice squad and logged 22 of 60 offensive snaps. He ran 13 routes on Geno Smith's 23 dropbacks and obviously made the most of his two targets. In his 120th career regular-season game, it was Shepard's first career two-touchdown performance. It's unlikely to be indicative of future performance.

11576.short: Allen rushed 16 times for 75 yards while catching his lone target for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
11576.long: Allen's 16 carries matched his total from the previous two games combined, as he had seen a downtick in opportunities since fellow RB Breece Hall returned from a quadriceps injury. Hall led the backfield once again with 100 scrimmage yards and a touchdown on 23 touches, but Allen was a key part of the game plan as well in the run-heavy win. The Jets will face a one-win team for a second consecutive game in Week 12 at Miami, which could allow Allen to stay involved alongside Hall.

1373.short: Smith completed 17 of 21 passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers. He also rushed once for four yards.
1373.long: Smith didn't have a completion longer than 21 yards but kept the offense on schedule with an accurate performance. Most importantly, he stepped up in the red zone, which has been the team's Achilles' heel throughout the season. Smith threw a seven-yard touchdown pass to Breece Hall to snap the Jets' two-game touchdown drought in the second quarter, then tacked on touchdown passes of eight and 15 yards to practice squad elevation Sterling Shepard. The veteran QB will take a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 12 road game against the Dolphins, who defeated the Jets in Week 7 despite three touchdown passes from Smith.

8146.short: Wilson caught three of five targets for 39 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
8146.long: Wilson led the team in receiving yards and targets as Geno Smith threw for just 176 yards, though Wilson wasn't on the receiving end of any of Smith's three touchdown passes. The Jets' No. 1 wideout hasn't scored since Week 5, and Wilson has fallen short of 45 receiving yards four times this season, though he has also topped 100 yards three times. Wilson will face a Dolphins defense in Week 12 that held him to a season-low 26 receiving yards in their Week 7 meeting.

8155.short: Hall rushed 20 times for 86 yards while catching all three of his targets for 14 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
8155.long: Hall reached 100 scrimmage yards for the second consecutive game while scoring his first touchdown since Week 1 on a seven-yard reception in the second quarter. Both Hall and Braelon Allen (17 touches for 84 yards) were heavily involved as the Jets snapped a five-game losing streak and were able to stick with the ground game. Hall has 56 touches to Allen's 36 in three games since the former returned from a quadriceps injury. After dropping the Chargers to 1-9 with Sunday's win, Hall and the Jets will face the 1-9 Dolphins in Week 12.

11724.short: Wallace (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
11724.long: Wallace will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a groin injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Nov. 29. He's mostly operated on special teams this season, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at the edge rusher position for Sunday's contest.

5049.short: Phillips (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
5049.long: Phillips played through an ankle issue against the Bills in Week 10, and the veteran defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up for Sunday's contest. He has accumulated 36 tackles (11 solo) and one fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games.

3281.short: Onyemata (abdomen) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
3281.long: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and strung together three consecutive limited practice sessions. However, the veteran defensive tackle is not quite ready to come off IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29. Onyemata has not played since Week 2 against the Packers due to an abdominal injury.

8395.short: Belton finished Sunday's loss to the Bills with six tackles (one solo) and one defensed pass.
8395.long: Belton tied for third on the Jets with six stops. That's a total he's now reached in every game this season except Week 1. Belton ranks second among NFL safeties with 82 tackles on the campaign.

1052.short: Davis posted six tackles (three solo) Sunday in a loss to Buffalo.
1052.long: Davis' six tackles tied for third-most on the Jets. The veteran linebacker has been relatively consistent this season with between six and 10 stops in seven of his 10 games so far. Davis has 68 total tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through 10 games, putting him on pace for a 10th consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign.

7841.short: Sherwood secured nine tackles (four solo) in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Bills.
7841.long: Sherwood finished second on the Jets in stops Sunday, behind Harrison Phillips (10). Sherwood has notched at least eight tackles in five straight games, and he's hit the double-digit mark three times this season. The veteran linebacker ranks eighth in the NFL with 86 tackles through 10 games.

5119.short: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts in the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
5119.long: Sanders knocked in field goals from 41, 27, 22 and 48 yards out in Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all 12 of the Jets' points for a second straight week, performing the same feat in the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs. Sanders moves to 25-for-28 on field-goal attempts over nine contests so far during the 2026 season.

13303.short: Klubnik completed 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills. He added three rushing attempts for 26 yards.
13303.long: Klubnik saw the first regular-season action of his NFL career in the second half of Sunday's loss, as Geno Smith (ankle) exited the game. The rookie fourth-round pick led the offense down to Buffalo's four-yard line on his first possession in the third quarter, but the Jets settled for a field goal on that possession, and Klubnik was picked off on his next drive. If Smith isn't ready to return in Week 11, Klubnik would be in line to make his first regular-season start on the road against the Chargers.

4195.short: Elliott went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
