4195.long: The Eagles' kicker accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, as he was good from 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards on his field goals. It was Elliott's first game with multiple field goals made since Week 4 against the Rams. That's how broken the Philadelphia offense has been for an extended period, and it doesn't project to get any better moving forward with Joe Milton at the controls. Elliott will be a hold-your-nose fantasy play in a theoretically high-scoring environment Thursday against the Cowboys, but it will be a movable force against a stoppable object when the Dallas defense squares off with the Eagles offense.

13294.short: Lemon caught one of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
13294.long: Lemon turned three targets into just three yards while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) paced the Eagles with 12 targets in the latter's return. In five games playing alongside Smith, Lemon has just 11 catches for 60 yards. Opportunities should be available against Dallas' porous secondary on Thanksgiving, but it remains to be seen if the unproven QB-WR combo of Joe Milton and Lemon can capitalize on that favorable matchup.

5022.short: Goedert caught his only target for 38 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
5022.long: Goedert turned his only look from Joe Milton into Philadelphia's longest pass play of the game. This was Goedert's second one-catch performance in eight appearances this season, but he recorded at least four receptions in each of the other six games. He hasn't scored a touchdown since a two-TD performance in the season opener, but perhaps a Thanksgiving matchup with the generous Dallas defense can help Goedert end that drought.

11557.short: Milton completed 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards while rushing five times for seven yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
11557.long: Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass or interception through two starts. He rushed for just seven yards Sunday after notching 64 rushing yards against the Giants in his first start with the Eagles, but Milton avoided mistakes as the Eagles rode their defense and Saquon Barkley's legs to their third win of the season. Twelve of Milton's 21 passes were directed to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in their first game together. Milton is poised to start on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys, with whom he appeared in four games last season. He was on Dallas' practice squad prior to signing with the Eagles in October.

4866.short: Barkley (left arm) said after Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers that he believes he'll play in Thursday's game at Dallas, Johnny McGonigal of PennLive.com reports.
4866.long: Barkley didn't log a touch after the 8:02 mark of the fourth quarter after he had an apparent left arm injury examined by team trainers, according to Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. While Barkley wouldn't elaborate on the issue to McGonigal, the running back seemed optimistic about his chances to suit up in Week 12. Barkley finished Sunday's matchup with 17 carries for 75 yards and one touchdown and wasn't targeted by QB Joe Milton. Monday's injury report may provide further clarity on Barkley's situation.

7525.short: Smith (hamstring) caught five of 12 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
7525.long: Smith was targeted on 12 of Joe Milton's 21 passes in the wide receiver's first game since Week 6. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass through two starts for the Eagles, so expectations should be tempered for the team's passing game as a whole, but Smith has reclaimed his role as the team's top pass catcher. Smith could make the most of his hefty target share Thursday against the generous Dallas secondary.

3415.short: Jones (foot) was spotted in a walking boot following Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
3415.long: Jones is dealing with an apparent right foot injury after recording five total tackles (two solo) and three passes defensed during the team's Week 11 victory. More information on his status will likely come when the Eagles return to practice Wednesday.

11662.short: Mitchell (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
11662.long: Mitchell injured his left hamstring in the second half, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for the third-year defensive back to be sidelined for the remainder of Sunday's contest. Riq Woolen will take over at cornerback the rest of the way.

11577.short: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
11577.long: Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

12667.short: Mondon (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's matchup against Pittsburgh.
12667.long: Mondon was deemed doubtful entering the weekend after not practicing Thursday or Friday following Philadelphia's Week 10 bye. He could have seen more action on defense after Zack Baun (back) landed on IR on Saturday, but Mondon will instead miss his first game of the campaign. Jeremiah Trotter and Jihaad Campbell figure to be the Eagles' starting inside linebackers Sunday.

13335.short: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday.
13335.long: As the emergency third quarterback, Payton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

10888.short: Carter (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
10888.long: Carter informed the Eagles' medical staff while he was traveling to the stadium Sunday that his quadriceps was bothering him. The fifth-year defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up, but if he plays under a snap count or is available only as an emergency option, then Ty Robinson and Gabe Hall would be poised to take on larger roles on defense.

6815.short: Baun (back) was placed on the Eagles' injured reserve Saturday.
6815.long: Baun was held out of practice all week due to a back injury that he sustained against the Giants in Week 9. The injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR, which means he'll miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 15 against the Seahawks. Jeremiah Trotter figures to start alongside Jihaad Campbell at inside linebacker moving forward, beginning with Sunday's home tilt against the Steelers.

9486.short: The Eagles placed Wicks (ankle/foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
9486.long: Wicks missed the three games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to an ankle injury, and he was limited during Week 11 prep before the team tacked on a foot issue on Friday's practice report, after which he was ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Steelers. Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Wicks sustained the foot injury Friday, and it presumably led to his placement on IR. Wicks will be sidelined until at least Philadelphia's Week 15 matchup with Seattle on Saturday, Dec. 19.

7835.short: Carter (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.
7835.long: An abdominal injury prevented Carter from playing in Week 9 against the Giants. He had extra rest thanks to the Week 10 bye, and his full practice Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Carter's return gives the Eagles a boost in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

10873.short: Smith (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
10873.long: An illness limited Smith's practice reps both Wednesday and Thursday, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year edge rusher has 17 tackles (nine solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass defense across eight regular-season games.

8414.short: Covey (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
8414.long: Covey was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep, but the veteran wide receiver has done enough to be cleared to return from a two-game absence due to a knee injury. He'll likely operate as the Eagles' top return option on kickoffs and punts while providing depth at wide receiver.

12566.short: Campbell (hamstring/quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
12566.long: Campbell was sidelined for each of the Eagles' two contests prior to the Week 10 bye due to hamstring and quadriceps injuries. The second-year linebacker made the most of the extra rest courtesy of the bye, and he is on track to return against the Steelers on Sunday.

9230.short: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
9230.long: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

12457.short: The Eagles signed Blue from their practice squad to their active roster Tuesday.
12457.long: It's already the third time this season Blue has been signed by Philadelphia from the practice squad to the active roster. The second-year pro has seen action in two games with the club, recording a nine-yard catch on his only touch while racking up 268 yards on 12 kickoff returns. Blue is currently the only healthy running back on the Eagles' active roster aside from starter Saquon Barkley, but that may change soon, as Will Shipley (foot - IR) had his practice window opened Monday. Elijah Mitchell has been promoted from the practice squad to help in the backfield each of the past three weeks, so he'd need to be signed to the active roster as well in order to suit up against Pittsburgh this Sunday.

1339.short: The Eagles signed Ertz from the practice squad to the active roster Monday.
1339.long: Philadelphia is coming off a Week 10 bye, but prior to the midseason respite, there were no reported injuries in the TE group on the active roster. When the position group was depleted earlier this season, the team used elevations on Ertz from Weeks 3-5, but his snap share decreased game by game (38, 21 and 11 percent), while he hauled in three of eight targets for 22 yards in that span. Wednesday's practice report will reveal if any of Dallas Goedert, Eli Stowers, Johnny Mundt or Grant Calcaterra are banged up at the moment.

11752.short: Trotter recorded 11 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants in Week 9.
11752.long: Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

9479.short: Washington caught all three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
9479.long: The big tight end earned just a 6.8 percent target share on a day Aaron Rodgers' fired off 44 pass attempts in prolonged comeback mode. Washington has been held to 25 yards or fewer in eight of 10 games this season. He doesn't see enough volume to warrant weekly fantasy consideration as a touchdown-or-bust bet.

7600.short: Freiermuth caught all five of his targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
7600.long: Freiermuth matched his season high in catches, securing five passes in a game for the third time this year. The tight end has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards in a contest this season, and he entered Week 11 with exactly two catches in each of the team's last four games. Freiermuth has now caught 32 of 43 targets for 309 yards and five touchdowns while also adding four rushes for five yards and a score over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

13200.short: Hurleman caught six of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles. He also had two kickoff returns for 32 yards and three punt returns for 36 yards.
13200.long: Hurleman unexpectedly emerged as Aaron Rodgers' go-to target during Pittsburgh's fourth-quarter comeback bid after DK Metcalf was disqualified. The practice squad elevation put an exclamation point on his NFL debut with a 20-yard touchdown catch with 1:21 left in the fourth quarter. Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson have all played prominent roles when available, and Michael Pittman (foot) could be back as soon as Friday against the Broncos, but Hurleman may have earned himself another elevation, and possibly even a continued role on offense, after leading the Steelers in receiving yards Sunday.

96.short: Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown while rushing five times for 29 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
96.long: Rodgers threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Max Hurleman on Pittsburgh's final offensive play with 1:21 remaining in the fourth quarter, but that was too little too late, as the Eagles proceeded to run out the clock to drop the Steelers to 6-4. Hurleman stepped up down the stretch in his first NFL game after starting wide receiver DK Metcalf was disqualified. Rodgers had a four-game stretch in which he threw 11 touchdown passes while posting at least 235 passing yards in each outing, but he has failed to reach that yardage total in any of his last four starts while recording only four TDs during the latter stretch. Snapping out of this recent funk won't be easy for Rodgers against the stout Broncos defense Friday.

7021.short: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
7021.long: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.

8228.short: Warren rushed nine times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
8228.long: Warren finished with 29 yards on 11 touches compared to 34 yards on nine touches for Rico Dowdle, as Pittsburgh's backfield duo was held quiet for a second consecutive game. After recording at least 73 scrimmage yards in eight consecutive games to start the season, Warren has produced just 75 yards without a touchdown over the past two games. Warren and Dowdle should continue to split backfield touches Friday against the Broncos.

5846.short: Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
5846.long: After accruing his second unsportsmanlike penalty of the contest, Metcalf was tossed from this Week 11 matchup. Prior to his exit with 4:58 remaining in the third quarter, he was having his least productive performance of the season (1-2-0 receiving line on four targets). The Steelers will roll with Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and Max Hurleman at wide receiver with Metcalf unavailable for the rest of the game.

7113.short: Highsmith (ankle) has been ruled out from returning to Sunday's matchup against Philadelphia, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
7113.long: Highsmith began the game with a flourish, recording 2.0 sacks in the first quarter. However, he injured his ankle during that opening period and isn't going to be able to re-enter the contest. Jack Sawyer will likely log more defensive snaps with Highsmith sidelined.

13491.short: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
13491.long: Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. Wetjen's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Broncos, although the rookie fourth-rounder's chances of suiting up for that contest would be further diminished if Michael Pittman (foot) is activated from IR before that game.

6807.short: Queen (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
6807.long: Queen was working through a hand injury during Week 11 prep, but the veteran linebacker has been given the green light by medical staff to play Sunday. He has logged double-digit tackles in each of his last three outings and is up to 74 tackles (25 solo), including 3.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including an interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

5071.short: Elliott (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
5071.long: Elliott did not play in Week 10 against the Bengals due to a knee injury he sustained during pregame warmups. He drew the questionable tag for Week 11 after logging full practices Thursday and Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. Elliott's return means Robert Spears-Jennings will revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

12511.short: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday.
12511.long: As has been the case all year, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. As such, Howard is not allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Rodgers and Rudolph leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

11630.short: Wilson (hand/finger) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
11630.long: The third-year wideout was activated from injured reserve Saturday, foreshadowing his availability for Sunday's contest following a four-game absence. Wilson recorded at least three receptions in his first four games of the season on his way to a 14-188-2 line on 25 targets, and he then failed to reel in the only pass thrown his way in Week 5 against the Colts before exiting that game at halftime with his injury. In his return Sunday against Philadelphia, Wilson should slot into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, the latter who leapfrogged Wilson on the depth chart over the last several games while filling in for both him and Michael Pittman (IR, foot).

6819.short: Pittman (foot) is not expected to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN reports.
6819.long: Pittman was able to practice fully both Thursday and Friday, but he is not ready to rejoin the mix just yet -- which Pittsburgh confirmed by omitting Pittman from the list of roster moves it made Saturday. Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive Black Friday, when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.

10940.short: Herbig (hip) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Burt Lauten of the Steelers' official site reports.
10940.long: A hip injury prevented Herbig from participating in any of the Steelers' three practice sessions during Week 11 prep. The door was left ajar for him to play Sunday, but he'll observe the game from the sidelines, and his absence means Jack Sawyer will operate in an elevated role at edge rusher behind starters Alex Highsmith and T.J. Watt. Herbig's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Broncos on Friday.

8323.short: Brisker notched 10 tackles (two solo) Sunday in a Week 10 loss to the Bengals.
8323.long: Pittsburgh gave up 38 points, so it wasn't exactly a stellar performance by the team's defense. However, three different Steelers players logged double-digit tackles -- including Brisker, who finished with 10. That's a season-high mark for the veteran safety, who has finished with at least six stops in all but one of his nine games so far this season.

11727.short: Wilson recorded 19 tackles (nine solo) in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
11727.long: Wilson not only set a career high with his 19 stops, he also tied the NFL high mark by any player so far this season. The third-year linebacker has jumped up a notch as an IDP asset in 2026, as he's tied for sixth in the league with 88 stops through nine games. Wilson has also added a sack, three defensed passes (including one interception) and a fumble recovery.

1945.short: Boswell made his sole field-goal attempt and sole PAT in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
1945.long: Boswell had an uneventful night, making his 45-yard field goal in the second quarter of the contest. The kicker moves to 19-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 17-for-17 on PATs over nine regular-season games in 2026.

13274.short: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
13274.long: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

13414.short: Black notched six carries for eight yards and secured his only target for seven yards during Sunday's 35-10 win versus the Vikings in Mexico City.
13414.long: Black entered Week 11 action on the heels of three consecutive contests with double-digit touches, so Sunday's performance was a step back to his modest outings from Weeks 2-6. In any case, the rookie third-round pick continues to be utilized regularly in the 49ers offense, averaging 9.1 touches for 37.8 yards from scrimmage per game while working as the clear No. 2 RB behind Christian McCaffrey. Black's next chance to contribute arrives next Sunday against the Seahawks.

5872.short: Samuel logged two carries for 27 yards, gathered in three of four targets for 20 yards and returned two kickoffs for 57 yards during Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City.
5872.long: Samuel didn't come close to replicating the 109 yards from scrimmage and two TDs on six touches that he accrued during a Week 10 shootout in Dallas, but he continued to mix into the offense in all realms, as he's ranged from two to eight touches in each of his seven appearances this season. Overall, he's averaging 11.7 yards per catch and a whopping 13.1 yards per carry to go with five total touchdowns in 2026, making him one big play away from producing weekly.

4217.short: Kittle caught all three of his targets for 34 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
4217.long: Kittle scored on both of his first-half catches, capping San Francisco's opening drive with a 17-yard touchdown before adding an eight-yard score in the first minute of the second quarter. The multi-touchdown performance was especially impressive considering the Vikings came in having allowed just one touchdown on a league-low 33 catches to tight ends. Kittle has been one of the top performers at his position as usual, with seven touchdown catches in 10 games, though his streak of consecutive outings with at least four catches ended at eight games. Up next for Kittle is a Week 12 home game against the Seahawks.

8183.short: Purdy completed 21 of 26 pass attempts for 255 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
8183.long: Purdy remained effective despite facing the vaunted Vikings defense, which had allowed just six touchdown passes through nine games. He threw touchdown passes on three of San Francisco's first four drives, connecting with George Kittle for scores of 17 and eight yards before finding Mike Evans for a four-yard touchdown in Evans' first action since Week 6 due to an Achilles injury. Purdy will take a stellar 23:5 TD:INT into another tough matchup on paper in Week 12 against the Seahawks, who held him to a season-low 189 passing yards in Week 5.

4034.short: McCaffrey rushed 12 times for 49 yards and a touchdown while catching both of his targets for 13 yards in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
4034.long: McCaffrey was relatively quiet in the lopsided win, but he extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a six-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. The versatile running back was much less involved as a pass catcher Sunday night after racking up 161 yards and two touchdowns through the air against the Cowboys in Week 10, and he finished with a season-low 62 scrimmage yards against the Vikings. Backup Kaelon Black had just eight rushing yards on his six carries after siphoning off at least 11 rushing attempts in each of the previous three games. McCaffrey is set to face another stout defensive front in Week 12 when the 49ers host the Seahawks, against whom McCaffrey churned out 83 scrimmage yards and a touchdown in Week 5.

6056.short: Greenlaw (neck) is inactive for Sunday night's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
6056.long: Greenlaw will be forced to miss Week 11 as a result of a neck injury that forced him to be less than 100 percent at practice throughout the week. In his absence, Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford are both candidates to take over as the team's primary weakside linebacker versus Minnesota.

12467.short: James (calf) is active for Sunday night's matchup with the Vikings, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
12467.long: James is good to go for Week 11 after dealing with a calf injury at practice late in the week. The running back will be available as a depth option in the backfield behind starter Christian McCaffrey and primary backup Kaelon Black versus Minnesota.

6864.short: Kareem (ankle) is inactive for Sunday night's game against the Vikings.
6864.long: Kareem has 12 tackles (six solo) across eight games this season as a rotational lineman and special-teams contributor.

7527.short: Jones (illness) is active for Sunday night's matchup against Minnesota, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
7527.long: Jones is good to go for Sunday Night Football after dealing with an illness at practice throughout the week. The quarterback will operate in his primary reserve role behind starter Brock Purdy versus the Vikings in Mexico City.

3286.short: Robinson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday night's contest against the Vikings, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
3286.long: Robinson will take a seat after appearing in each of the team's last two contests. With Mike Evans returning to action Sunday night after missing three contests with an Achilles injury, Robinson is the odd man out in the 49ers' WR room.

2216.short: Evans (Achilles) is listed as active Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
2216.long: Evans thus is poised for his first game action since Week 6 versus the Commanders after missing the 49ers' last three contests due to right Achilles tendinitis. As for Evans' potential workload, Jay Glazer reported on Fox NFL Sunday that the wide receiver likely will avoid a strict "pitch count," but San Francisco also plans to "be smart" with his snaps. Even a limited Evans is viable for fantasy purposes, but he'll have to contend with RB Christian McCaffrey, TE George Kittle and active WRs Deebo Samuel, Keenan Allen, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing for the attention of QB Brock Purdy.

7823.short: Hobbs (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday night's game against the Vikings.
7823.long: The veteran cornerback remains on injured reserve but had been listed as questionable. He had his 21-day practice window opened 17 days ago, so the 49ers will need to make a decision on Hobbs next week. He's yet to play in a game this season.

12649.short: The 49ers activated West (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.
12649.long: The Niners also removed West's questionable tag, so he should be ready to play Sunday night against Minnesota. West played 41 percent of the defensive snaps during the first two weeks of the season before suffering his knee injury.

10936.short: Brown (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
10936.long: Brown opened the week with back-to-back limited practices due to an ankle issue, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year safety has 51 tackles (28 solo) and three pass defenses in nine regular-season games.

11697.short: Green (back) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
11697.long: Green was not able to finish the 49ers' win over the Cowboys in Week 10 because of his back injury, but it now seems like he's back to 100 percent. He projects to play a significant role in San Francisco's secondary during Sunday's game against Minnesota.

11651.short: Guerendo (pectoral) was working off to the side during practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
11651.long: Guerendo has been on the PUP list with a pec injury since training camp, but it now looks like he may be making some progress toward returning to action. Even if he does get back to full strength at some point soon, though, it's not clear how much room there will be for him in a 49ers' backfield that has recently been dominated by veteran Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black.

4950.short: Kirk announced Wednesday via his personal Instagram account that he recently underwent meniscus surgery.
4950.long: After he had missed the 49ers' first six games of the season while recovering from a calf injury, Kirk landed on injured reserve for the second time this season back on Nov. 7 due to a right knee injury sustained in his team debut Week 7 in Atlanta. Since Kirk didn't specify whether he required a partial meniscectomy or a meniscus repair, his exact recovery timeline isn't known. Regardless, he'll have to miss at least two more games while he's on IR.

13417.short: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
13417.long: This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

6803.short: Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said Tuesday that the receiver is "100 percent healthy" and fully recovered from his November 2024 right knee surgery and plans to work out for interested teams once he's released by the 49ers, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
6803.long: After Aiyuk filed his paperwork for reinstatement, San Francisco activated him from the reserve/left squad list Nov. 9. Rosenhaus noted that Aiyuk passed his physical at that time, with MRIs and X-rays on his surgically repaired knee revealing no concerns. The 49ers were granted a two-week roster exemption for Aiyuk that will expire next Monday, and the 28-year-old wideout is expected to be cut loose at that time since San Francisco seemingly hasn't expressed interested in retaining him. While it's unclear what kind of market might exist for Aiyuk's services coming off a lengthy layoff from NFL action, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relayed earlier this month that at least one NFC team has expressed interest in adding the receiver to its practice squad.

10891.short: Witherspoon logged four solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
10891.long: Coach Mike MacDonald dialed up the blitz against rookie first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza in his first career start. Two of Witherspoon's four tackles in the Seahawks' win came behind the line of scrimmage off cornerback blitzes against Mendoza. Witherspoon also played all 59 of the team's defensive snaps in the one-score win.

7672.short: Jones logged 10 tackles (five solo) in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
7672.long: Jones helped make first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza's NFL debut miserable. The inside linebacker helped the Seahawks' defense contain the young quarterback's scrambling ability while also limiting his mid-range opportunities from the pocket en route to yet another defensive win for the defending champs.

2747.short: Myers missed his sole field-goal attempt and made three PATs in the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
2747.long: Myers missed a 44-yard field-goal attempt with 7:05 remaining in the game that would have put the Seahawks up 14 points. The kicker is now 16-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 21-for-23 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

4039.short: Kupp hauled in his lone target for a 34-yard touchdown during the Seahawks' 21-13 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
4039.long: It was the third time this season that Kupp recorded only one catch, but the veteran wide receiver made his lone reception count when he found open space on a broken play to connect with Drew Lock for a TD late in the first quarter. It was the third touchdown catch of the season for Kupp, two of which have come over his last three outings. He'll enter the bye with a 23-272-3 line on 35 targets through 10 regular-season games, and the Seahawks' next matchup will take place in Week 12 on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

12497.short: Horton failed to garner a target during Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
12497.long: Horton failed to reel in a pass for the first time since Week 7, and his 10 offensive snaps ranked fourth at wide receiver for Seattle behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43), Cooper Kupp (35) and Rashid Shaheed (25). Horton will continue to be an unappealing fantasy option as long as he's buried below the other three wideouts on the depth chart.

12048.short: Holani is week-to-week after suffering an MCL sprain in Sunday's win over Las Vegas, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday.
12048.long: Holani exited Sunday's Week 10 game against the Raiders after suffering a knee injury. The 26-year-old is not currently expected to be placed on injured reserve, but he will be reevaluated after Seattle's Week 11 bye. The three-year pro has had a larger role on special teams since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned from injuries to helm Seattle's ground attack.

4943.short: Head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that he's "really optimistic" Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) will be able to get a full week's worth of practice coming out of the Seahawks' Week 11 bye and start their next game Sunday, Nov. 29, against the 49ers, John Boyle of the team's official site reports.
4943.long: Darnold, who last played in Week 8, still is working his way through a pair of injuries, but barring any setbacks, he's trending toward a Week 12 return. Macdonald reiterated that Darnold will be the team's starter once healthy, even though backup Drew Lock has guided Seattle to a 4-0 record while coming on in relief or starting in place of an injured Darnold in the first two games of the season as well as the most recent two contests.

11603.short: Barner caught all three targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
11603.long: Barner has been held below 25 receiving yards in eight of 10 games this season and has more rushing touchdowns (two) than receiving scores (one) during the 2026 campaign. He's the definition of a low-floor, touchdown-or-bust fantasy option headed into the team's bye week.

8676.short: Shaheed caught one pass for eight yards on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 win over the Raiders.
8676.long: After missing the previous two games with a knee injury, Shaheed returned against Las Vegas and maintained his role as the WR3 for Seattle. He played 25 of 57 offensive snaps and remained a non-factor in the box score. Shaheed has yet to hit 70 receiving yards in a game this season and has zero touchdowns as a pass catcher. He's off the fantasy radar.

5854.short: Lock completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and logged six carries for 20 yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory in Las Vegas.
5854.long: Lock took advantage of having WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba at his disposal, targeting him 10 times, one of which resulted in a 71-yard TD connection. Moreover, Lock also hooked up with Cooper Kupp on a sliding 34-yard touchdown, marking his second multi-TD outing in four appearances (three starts) this season. There's an expectation that Seahawks No. 1 QB Sam Darnold (quadriceps) returns from a two-game absence after the team's Week 11 bye, but until he receives a clean bill of health, Lock has a chance to be under center on the road against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

13286.short: Price posted nine carries for 36 yards and one touchdown and gathered in his only target for eight yards during Sunday's 21-13 victory at Las Vegas.
13286.long: This marks Price's fewest touches in a game since returning from IR in Week 8, and he actually was doubled up in the category by position mate Zach Charbonnet, who turned his 20 rushes into 94 yards. Having said that, Price salvaged his day with a 12-yard TD, the first of his career, on the ground in the third quarter. The breakdown of work between the two may signal what's to come in the Seahawks backfield after the team's Week 11 bye, with Price and company set to face off with the NFC West-leading 49ers on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

9753.short: Charbonnet churned out 94 yards on 20 carries during Sunday's 21-13 win in Las Vegas.
9753.long: Charbonnet was eased in to the mix in Weeks 8 and 9, going from nine touches in the first contest to 17 in the latter. This time around, though, he doubled up fellow RB Jadarian Price in touches (10) and more than did so in terms from yards from scrimmage (44). It may signal that Charbonnet is the Seahawks' clear-cut No. 1 backfield option moving forward, but he won't have a chance to prove as much until after the team's Week 11 bye on Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

9488.short: Smith-Njigba gathered in eight of 10 targets for 171 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 21-13 win at Las Vegas.
9488.long: Smith-Njigba's Week 10 performance was fueled by a 71-yard catch and run for a touchdown in the middle of the third quarter, but he still was able to put up 100 yards on his other seven receptions en route to a new season high in the category. As the Seahawks hit their Week 11 bye, he's reached the century mark in receiving eight times and resides on a 79-1,207-10 line on 109 targets through 10 contests. Smith-Njigba's next chance to continue aggravating opposing defenses arrives Sunday, Nov. 29, at San Francisco.

3220.short: Reed is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against Las Vegas due to a toe injury.
3220.long: Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

11435.short: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game at Arizona.
11435.long: Since Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price returned to the lineup in Week 8 against the Bears, Wilson was contained to special teams in that contest and then was active but didn't log a snap last Sunday versus the Cardinals. Now, Wilson will yield all the RB reps to Charbonnet, Price and George Holani in Week 10.

11396.short: Pili (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
11396.long: Pili missed the Seahawks' last two games while nursing a back injury, but he's been cleared to play in Week 10 after logging a full practice session Friday. His return gives the Seahawks more depth on the interior defensive line behind Byron Murphy.

5061.short: Nwosu (ankle) does not have an injury designation against the Raiders on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
5061.long: Nwosu has missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to an ankle injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after ending Week 10 prep with a full practice Friday. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and Connor O'Toole.

10911.short: Hall (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
10911.long: Hall was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 10 prep before sitting out Friday's session. However, his reduced practice reps appear to have been planned by the Seahawks to manage his back injury, and the fourth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. Hall has 24 tackles (14 solo), including 3.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

9506.short: Tucker didn't record any stats during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
9506.long: Tucker didn't garner any touches on offense for the third straight week as Tampa Bay opted to use Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell exclusively in the backfield. Tucker will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as both Irving and Gainwell are available for the Buccaneers.

8111.short: Otton caught one pass for eight yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
8111.long: The tight end earned just a 9.1 percent target share and continues to be nearly invisible in the box score despite being an every-down player who runs virtually every pass route for the Bucs. Otton has just one touchdown since Week 11 of the 2024 season and has just one career 100-yard receiving game across 73 regular-season contests. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet who clearly busts far more than he hits.

4037.short: Godwin caught three passes for 18 yards on three targets in Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
4037.long: The veteran wideout ran a team-high 41 routes on Baker Mayfield's 44 dropbacks, but Godwin continues to produce very little with his immense playing time. He's been held under 40 receiving yards in eight straight games and has yet to have a 50-yard receiving game this season. Godwin also has zero touchdowns. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option headed into next Monday night's date with the Panthers.

13317.short: Hurst caught five of seven targets for 56 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 31-21 loss to the Lions.
13317.long: Hurst led the team in targets and his five catches and 56 receiving yards were new season highs for the rookie. The wide receiver was able to reach paydirt twice, reeling in a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Baker Mayfield in the second quarter before the pair connected for a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. Hurst has now caught 16 of 32 targets for 224 yards and three touchdowns over 10 contests this season.

7567.short: Gainwell rushed four times for 16 yards and brought in four of five targets for 43 yards in the Buccaneers 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
7567.long: Gainwell held his usual complementary role on the ground behind a busy Bucky Irving, yet with the Buccaneers trailing throughout the second half, Gainwell was able to finish second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day for Tampa Bay. The veteran back has back-to-back 16-yard efforts on the ground, but Gainwell has a combined 7-103-0 line through the air in that same span heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

12514.short: Egbuka brought in two of five targets for 18 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
12514.long: Egbuka couldn't do much despite tying for the second-most targets on the afternoon for the Buccaneers. The 2025 first-round pick's catch total tied his season low, and he also posted his third sub-20-yard tally of the season. Egbuka has now been under 50 receiving yards in five consecutive contests heading into a Week 12 Monday night home showdown against the Panthers on Nov. 30.

4892.short: Mayfield completed 20 of 33 passes for 187 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed six times for 36 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Tampa Bay.
4892.long: Mayfield fought through foot and thumb injuries to take the field in a critical game for the 3-6 Buccaneers, but he wasn't able to keep pace with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. Mayfield did throw multiple touchdown passes for the first time this season, hitting rookie Ted Hurst for scoring strikes of 23 and four yards. Mayfield's rushing yardage total was also a new season high, and he'll next take aim at the Panthers' beatable secondary in a Week 12 divisional home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 30.

11584.short: Irving rushed 18 times for 68 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 32 yards in the Buccaneers' 31-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
11584.long: Irving worked hard all afternoon against a feisty Lions defense, and outside of his game-long 23-yard run, he scuffled to 45 yards on 17 carries. Irving worked around a hard shot to the abdomen that he sustained in the second half, and he did manage to contribute a rushing touchdown for the fourth straight game when he went in from one yard out in the latter portion of the third quarter. Irving has now equaled a career high with eight rushing touchdowns, and he's 107 yards short of his second career 1,000-yard season on the ground heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Panthers on Monday night, Nov. 30.

12576.short: Morrison (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against Detroit, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
12576.long: Morrison was ruled out by Tampa Bay during the second half. He'll finish the contest with four tackles (three solo). Jacob Parrish (back) has also been ruled out for the remainder of the game, so Kevin Knowles has entered at cornerback for the Bucs.

12605.short: Parrish (back) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Lions.
12605.long: Parrish's back injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Benjamin Morrison will continue to operate in an elevated role in the secondary in Parrish's absence.

10921.short: Diaby is active for Sunday's matchup against Detroit, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
10921.long: Diaby was inactive in Week 9 due to a knee injury. Now coming off the bye week, the 27-year-old is ready to fit back into his starting linebacker role. He has 16 tackles (11 solo), including 3.0 sacks and two pass breakups, including one interception, through eight regular-season games.

6185.short: Stick (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Lions, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
6185.long: The Buccaneers elevated Stick from the team's practice squad Monday. The 31-year-old will only be eligible to play should both Baker Mayfield and Jalon Daniels exit with an injury, illness or ejection.

13425.short: Daniels is set for his usual role as Tampa Bay's backup quarterback Sunday versus Detroit, as Baker Mayfield (foot/thumb) is active and will start, Scott Smith of the Buccaneers' official site reports.
13425.long: Mayfield entered Sunday deemed questionable due to his injuries, but he's ultimately going to be able to suit up. As such, Daniels will retain his role as Mayfield's backup. Easton Stick (coach's decision) is serving as Tampa Bay's emergency third quarterback.

10999.short: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions.
10999.long: Hayes was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, but he is not quite ready to return from a knee procedure that he underwent in late August. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Panthers on Monday, Nov. 30.

11705.short: Smith recorded seven tackles (four solo) and an interception in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
11705.long: As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.

8384.short: McCollum recorded five tackles (four solo) and two interceptions in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
8384.long: The cornerback has been on an absolute heater in the interceptions department, as he's now recorded at least one pick in three straight games. After picking off Bryce Young and Michael Penix in back-to-back games, McCollum got Caleb Williams twice in Week 9. The four interceptions are a new career high for the fifth-year defensive back, who is now up to 35 tackles (28 solo), 11 pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.

4118.short: Anzalone posted two solo tackles and an interception during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.
4118.long: The Buccaneers picked off Caleb Williams four times, which included Anzalone's pick late in the third quarter that set up Tampa Bay in Chicago territory. Anzalone recorded four interceptions over his first nine NFL seasons, but he's already up to four picks in 2026, three of which have come over his last two outings. He enters the Week 10 bye with 44 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, through nine regular-season games.

13379.short: Trotter recorded eight tackles (five solo) during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.
13379.long: Trotter led the Buccaneers in tackles in Week 9, when he played 59 of 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent). The rookie second-rounder has logged at least six stops in each of the first eight games of the regular season, and he enters the Week 10 bye with 76 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass defenses (including a pick-six).

11994.short: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
11994.long: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

12485.short: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
12485.long: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

12502.short: Helm caught two of three targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
12502.long: The tight end has yet to catch a touchdown this season and was unable to get anything going against arguably the league's worst defense Sunday. Helm has been held below 30 receiving yards in nine of 10 games this season. He's nothing more than a low-end TE2 in fantasy.

12540.short: Dike caught six of seven targets for 69 yards during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
12540.long: Dike was able to reel in multiple passes for the third straight game, and his six snags set a new season high for the second-year pro. The 24-year-old paced the team in targets Sunday, narrowly edging out fellow wide receivers Calvin Ridley (six) and Carnell Tate (five). Dike will have a chance to continue carving out a more substantial role for himself on offense moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the rest of the 2026 campaign.

4981.short: Ridley caught five of six targets for 68 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys.
4981.long: Ridley reeled in multiple passes in a contest for the first time since Week 5, and his 12-yard touchdown connection with Cam Ward in the fourth quarter was the wideout's first score of the year. Ridley trailed only fellow wide receiver Chimere Dike (seven) in targets, and Ridley could continue to see added opportunities moving forward with Wan'Dale Robinson (ankle) sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

12522.short: Ward completed 21 of 30 passes for 248 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for three yards and another score in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
12522.long: Ward's final line belies his struggles somewhat, as a Cowboys defense that made a defensive playcaller switch brought him down for five sacks and forced a lost fumble on one of them at Dallas' 20-yard line. Ward did manage to connect with Carnell Tate (59 yards) and Calvin Ridley (12 yards) for his pair of TD passes, the first coming when the rookie wideout alertly got up after not being touched and the second on a broken play where Ward threw across the field after buying several extra seconds with his legs. Ward also had a one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter, and despite Tennessee's team-level misery, the second-year signal-caller has thrown for at least 231 yards and two touchdowns in three consecutive games heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

13279.short: Tate brought in two of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
13279.long: Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

5967.short: Pollard rushed 21 times for 110 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Titans' 51-30 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
5967.long: Pollard eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the third time in the last four games, lighting up his old team for multiple productive gains on the afternoon. The veteran back has been a bright spot in a dismal 1-9 start for Tennessee, despite game script often working against the ground attack in the second halves of the Titans' contests. Pollard remains firmly on pace for a fifth straight 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

7036.short: Burgess (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
7036.long: Burgess injured his knee early in the second half, and he will be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. He was filling in for Tony Adams (illness) at safety, so Isaiah Oliver is the next man up for the Titans.

8310.short: Flott (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against Dallas, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
8310.long: Flott was hurt with just under six minutes remaining in the first half while tackling CeeDee Lamb. He was evaluated on the sideline and subsequently deemed questionable to return. Micah Robinson entered at cornerback in Flott's stead.

8860.short: Adams (illness) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
8860.long: Adams was added to the Titans' injury report right before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff due to the illness, and the veteran safety wasn't able to take any snaps before being ruled out for Sunday's contest. Terrell Burgess drew the start at safety alongside Kevin Winston in Adams' absence, per Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com.

13288.short: Singleton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
13288.long: Week 11 marks the fifth time in six games that Singleton will be a healthy scratch, despite the fact that Tyjae Spears (knee) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. As such, Michael Carter and Julius Chestnut will operate as the Titans' rotational options in the backfield behind workhorse running back Tony Pollard on Sunday. Singleton's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Jaguars on Nov. 29.

13365.short: Hill (neck) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas.
13365.long: Hill didn't play in Week 10 against the Jaguars, marking his first absence of the 2026 campaign. He logged a full practice Friday but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation. However, the rookie is cleared to suit up in Week 11 for the meeting with the Cowboys, potentially resulting in fewer snaps for Dorian Mausi.

11835.short: Harrell (knee) was taken to a hospital in Tampa on Saturday following a serious car accident, Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com reports.
11835.long: Harrell is being monitored following Saturday's accident. The third-year pro tore his ACL in a preseason game against the 49ers in mid-August, which led to him being placed on season-ending injured reserve.

7607.short: The Titans elevated Carter from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
7607.long: The elevation of Carter gives the Titans extra depth at running back following the placement of Tyjae Spears (knee) on injured reserve. Carter -- who has appeared in three regular-season games for Tennessee -- is listed as the fourth running back on the depth chart behind Tony Pollard, Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton.

9508.short: The Titans placed Spears (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
9508.long: Spears was sidelined for Weeks 7 and 8 due to a knee injury but was cleared to play against the Jaguars in Week 10, when he turned four carries into 28 yards and failed to haul in his lone target. He was initially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys after logging a full practice Friday, but the Titans have determined that a stint on injured reserve is warranted for the fourth-year running back. Spears will be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next chance to play is Week 15 against the Colts on Sunday, Dec. 20. Tony Pollard will continue to be the workhorse running back for the Titans while Julius Chestnut and rookie fifth-rounder Nicholas Singleton provide depth out of the backfield.

12588.short: Winston (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
12588.long: Winston's practice reps were limited Thursday due to a shoulder issue, but he was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag heading into the weekend. The second-year safety has 56 tackles (31 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games.

6065.short: Barton (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Dallas.
6065.long: Barton strung together three consecutive full practices, and the lack of an injury tag indicates that the veteran linebacker has cleared the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing against the Jaguars in Week 10. Barton's return means less defensive snaps may be available for Dorian Mausi, although the latter could start at linebacker if Anthony Hill (neck) is not cleared to play against the Cowboys on Sunday.

5466.short: Franklin-Myers (back) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
5466.long: Franklin-Myers appeared on the Titans' injury report with a back issue Wednesday, but it doesn't seem like it was anything too severe. He should again play a prominent role on Tennessee's defensive line in a Week 11 tilt against the Cowboys.

11742.short: Gray posted nine tackles (eight solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Titans' 40-23 loss to the Jaguars in Week 10.
11742.long: Gray was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a concussion. The third-year linebacker led the Titans in both total and solo tackles, and he also picked off a pass from Trevor Lawrence intended for Jakobi Meyers midway through the first quarter, although Tennessee's offense was not able to convert that takeaway into points. Gray is up to 46 tackles (26 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and two pass defenses (one interception) through eight regular-season games.

10903.short: Martin (shoulder) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.
10903.long: Martin's practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder issue, but his full session Saturday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Monday night's game. Martin could see an uptick in defensive snaps if defensive back Amik Robertson (ankle) is not cleared to play against Cincinnati.

6896.short: Robertson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Bengals.
6896.long: Robertson injured his ankle on the final play of Friday's practice, and his reps were limited during Saturday's session. If he's not cleared to play, then Mike Sainristil and Quan Martin would both be in line for more snaps in the Commanders' secondary.

12533.short: Croskey-Merritt (groin) is slated to be activated from IR in time to play in Monday's game against the Bengals, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
12533.long: Croskey-Merritt has missed the Commanders' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury. He logged a trio of full practices this week and is officially questionable to play Monday, but it sounds like he'll be activated from IR ahead of the contest and make his return against the Bengals. During Croskey-Merritt's absence, Rachaad White has taken on a larger role in the backfield, but White is currently dealing with a heel injury and is also questionable to suit up Monday.

8135.short: Burks (foot) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Bengals.
8135.long: Burks was held out of Friday's practice while managing a foot injury, but he returned Saturday as a full participant, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag for Monday's contest. Over his last six outings, Burks has caught 14 passes on 24 targets for 260 yards and two touchdowns, and he has operated as operated as the Commanders' WR3 since Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in Week 6 against the 49ers.

8136.short: White (heel) is listed as questionable for Monday's game versus the Bengals.
8136.long: White was added to the Commanders' Week 11 injury report Friday as limited due to a heel issue, and he followed it up with a DNP one day later before getting tagged ahead of Monday's matchup. At the same time, current IR member Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) completed a full week of drills and also is listed as questionable. If he's activated by Monday afternoon, he'll vie with Austin Ekeler and White for touches, assuming the latter avoids inactive status about 90 minutes before an 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

11942.short: Yankoff (knee) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
11942.long: Yankoff sat out the Commanders' contest against the Giants in Week 10 because of a knee injury, but it now looks like he's put it behind him. He figures to resume a depth role at tight end in Week 11 against the Bengals.

11650.short: McCaffrey returned two punts for 13 yards and three kickoffs for 58 yards in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.
11650.long: Though he's been active for five straight games while the Commanders' receiving depth has taken hits due to season-ending injuries to Terry McLaurin (knee) and Jaylin Lane (ankle), McCaffrey has yet to carve out much of a role on offense. He took the field for a season-high 14 of the Commanders' 69 offensive plays in Week 10 but went without a target. McCaffrey is likely to continue to provide his greatest impact on special teams, where he appears to have settled in as the Commanders' top return man on both kickoffs and punts.

5792.short: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
5792.long: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.

8392.short: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).
8392.long: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.

5580.short: Luvu recorded six tackles (two solo) and a forced fumble during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
5580.long: Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.

13375.short: Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
13375.long: Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).

13968.short: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.
13968.long: Stevens began the scoring in the contest with a 46-yard field goal early in the second period. That ended up being his only FG try of the game, but he made all three of his PATs. Stevens continued what has been a mostly fine rookie campaign -- he's made 17 of 20 field-goal attempts, with all three of his misses coming from 50-plus yards. However, he's just 15-for-18 on point-after tries.

11596.short: Sinnott caught all four of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown Thursday in a 24-21 victory against the Giants.
11596.long: Sinnott gave the Commanders a lead just before halftime when he reeled in a one-yard touchdown from Jayden Daniels. It was his first TD of the season and the third of his career. Sinnott's four grabs came out of nowhere, as he'd logged just one catch on two targets through his first eight games of the season. He also ranked third among Washington tight ends Thursday with 24 offensive snaps -- behind Chig Okonkwo (41) and John Bates (28) -- so fantasy managers probably don't need to go rushing to the waiver wire to pick him up. With that said, Sinnott may have earned himself more opportunities with Thursday's effort.

13301.short: Williams secured both targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
13301.long: Williams was a distant second to Stefon Diggs in receiving yards for the Commanders on the night, but like the latter, the former was on the receiving end of one of Jayden Daniels' three touchdown passes. Williams scored from 31 yards out just past the midway point of the third quarter, his first touchdown since way back in Week 1 against the Eagles. Williams hasn't been able to fully take advantage of the absence of Terry McLaurin (knee, IR) as of yet, but Thursday's score is certainly an encouraging sign heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

4663.short: Ekeler rushed nine times for 26 yards and brought in all four targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
4663.long: As his final line indicates, Ekeler retained a solid level of involvement in the narrow win, logging a season-high 13 touches. He posted a new season high in receiving yards along the way, and the veteran back has proven to be a solid complement to Rachaad White while Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin, IR) has been sidelined. However, with the latter potentially set to return as soon as Week 11's home matchup against the Bengals, Ekeler could be headed to a reduced role.

2449.short: Diggs secured six of 10 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
2449.long: Diggs paced the Commanders across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 32-yard catch-and-run touchdown grab over the middle with under a minute remaining sealed the win for Washington. Diggs tied a season high with his catch total while setting a new 2026 high-water mark in receiving yards and targets as well, and the veteran wideout should retain a prominent role throughout the second half of the season with Terry McLaurin (IR, knee) out the rest of the way in 2026. Diggs next takes aim at the Bengals' inconsistent secondary in a Week 11 home matchup on Monday night, Nov. 22.

11566.short: Daniels completed 23 of 33 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions and rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
11566.long: It was a up-and-down night for Daniels in the narrow division win, as the third-year quarterback's pair of fourth-quarter interceptions threatened to derail Washington's fortunes. Daniels had the Commanders up by a 17-14 score just past the midway point of the third quarter after tossing one- and 31-yard touchdown passes to Ben Sinnott and Antonio Williams, respectively. However, Daniels subsequently squandered one scoring opportunity by throwing interceptions on back-to-back possessions in the fourth quarter, the first at the Giants' two-yard line. He ultimately made up for it with his game-winning 32-yard scoring strike to Stefon Diggs, marking the quarterback's first three-TD-pass tally of the season. Daniels is up to 1,499 passing yards and a 10:2 TD:INT alongside 280 rushing yards and another pair of scores heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Bengals on Monday night, Nov. 23.

8210.short: Okonkwo (back) returned to Thursday's eventual 24-21 win at the Giants, finishing with four catches (on eight targets) for 24 yards.
8210.long: Okonkwo exited in the second quarter due to a back injury, but he was back out there on the field after halftime and was the target on both of Jayden Daniels' two interceptions with less than six minutes remaining in the contest. Overall, Okonkwo's eight targets marked a season high, but he also mustered his fewest receiving yards since Week 4. He'll look to build upon his season-long line of 27-263-0 on 39 targets in the Commanders' next game Monday, Nov. 23 versus the Bengals.
